Lee Trevino. The Merry Mex. A Mexican-American professional golfer who won 6 major championships and established himself as one of the most charismatic and entertaining competitors in golf. His folksy humor and exceptional ball-striking made him a fan favorite from the 1960s through the 1980s.

He won 6 major championships: 2 US Opens in 1968 and 1971, 2 PGA Championships in 1974 and 1984, and 2 Open Championships in 1971 and 1972. During 1971, he won three major championships in five weeks—the US Open, The Open Championship, and the Canadian Open—a remarkable streak. Trevino was known for his remarkable consistency off the tee and an unorthodox swing that generated exceptional accuracy. He was famous for his comedy and accessibility to fans, earning sponsorships and television popularity through his charismatic personality.

In 1975, he was struck by lightning during an event, suffering serious injuries but recovering to continue his career with undiminished competitiveness. He won 29 PGA Tour events and remained competitive on the Senior PGA Tour well into his later years. Trevino pioneered the path for Latino players in professional golf, becoming a cultural icon and ambassador for the sport. He shared an era with Tom Watson and Jack Nicklaus as rival competitors, and followed Arnold Palmer as a predecessor who influenced the accessibility standard for golfers.
